newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South-North Korea Red Cross talks proposal stalls.
newsitem.headline: South-North Korea Red Cross talks proposal stalls.

text.p: North Korea's Red Cross on Monday again rejected a proposal by its Southern counterpart that talks on speeding up food aid be held in the border village of Panmunjom.
The proposal was made by the head of the South Korean Red Cross, Kang Young-hoon, on April 18.
The Northern side said it would welcome talks and proposed May 3. But it insisted discussions be held in Beijing.
In a reply last Thursday, Kang said there was no need for Koreans to meet in a third country and proposed a working-level session in Panmunjom on Tuesday.
On Monday, the North Korean Red Cross reiterated its position in a message relayed via a telephone hot-line at Panmunjom, the South Korea Red Cross said in a statement.
North Korea is on the edge of famine after two consecutive years of devastating floods.
Meanwhile, the Southern group said on Monday it would ship 110 tonnes of wheat flour, worth 36 million won ($40,300), to its North Korean counterpart around Wednesday.
The wheat flour was bought with money raised by a South Korean Christian group.
The statement said the South Korean Red Cross had sent 16 shipments of food and garments to its Northern counterpart.
The two Koreas remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
